proposals.before: Court fired Hao Jia east to whip generals.
proposals.after: Therefore the court dispatched supervising secretary Hao Jia as a mobile headquarters to spur the offensive.
proposals.reason: 遣 means dispatched; “fired” wrongly suggests dismissal. Restore 治書御史…為行台 and the order to press the attack.

proposals.before: Handsome Liu Yin of Donglai, Qi royal blood, dazzled coastal elites.
proposals.after: Liu Yin, courtesy Chengyin, of Ye in Donglai—descendant of Han Prince Dao-Hui of Qi—was handsome and self-assured, befriended the magnates of his day, and won fame between the sea and Mount Tai so that scholars all admired him.
proposals.reason: Idiomatic omitted 字承胤, 掖, Han Qi ancestry detail, 交結時豪, and 士咸慕之; restore the Chinese propositions present in the sealed literal.

proposals.before: Xiong’s generals shattered Zhao at Warm Water; Wang Zai handed twin prefectures to Cheng.
proposals.after: Li Xiong sent Li Xiang and Ren Hui against Zhao; Zhao joined Hanjia administrator Wang Zai from southern Qin to resist them, fought at Warm Water, was routed, and Zai then surrendered both commanderies to Xiong.
proposals.reason: Idiomatic collapsed named commanders 李驤、任回 and Zhao’s joint resistance with Wang Zai into “Xiong’s generals”; restore the Chinese agents and outcome.

proposals.before: Bandits harried their march beyond a year.
proposals.after: Traveling with Meng, they met bandits on the road and took more than a year to arrive.
proposals.reason: Idiomatic omitted companion 孟 and the road encounter; restore both propositions from the Chinese.

proposals.before: Tyrants fell before Liu Bang’s plain cap;
